newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Minister says Indonesia deserves own peace prize.
newsitem.headline: Minister says Indonesia deserves own peace prize.

text.p: An Indonesian minister said on Saturday his country deserved the Nobel peace prize for its role in promoting regional stability in Southeast Asia during the last 30 years.

Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie said the 1996 Nobel peace prize, awarded to East Timor Bishop Carlos Belo and exiled resistance spokesman Jose Ramos-Horta, was not objective and made by five people who had never been to Indonesia.

Belo and Ramos-Horta were jointly awarded the prize earlier this month for their efforts towards securing a peaceful solution to the issue of East Timor, a former Portuguese colony that Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year.
"If there are people who deserve it, it is the people of Indonesia who have contributed to stability here," Habibie, speaking to German reporters ahead of the visit of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said.
"Can you imagine if Indonesia did not have a stable political climate? It would have an immediate effect on neighbouring countries in this region like Australia and Singapore," Habibie said.
"So when a prize has to be given to Indonesia, it has to be given to all the people of Indonesia who have accomplished this together," he said.
Kohl, who arrives in Indonesia on Saturday with a delegation of around 70 business people, is making an official one-day state visit on Monday which is expected to focus on economic issues.
He is due to spend Sunday fishing with Indonesian President Suharto near islands off Jakarta.
Ramos-Horta on Friday urged Kohl to press Suharto to begin withdrawing troops from East Timor.
Jakarta's annexation of the tiny territory has never been recognised by the United Nations, which regards Portugal as its administering power.
